cemc-galois-2006-01a.prompt:
A hat contains six slips of paper numbered from $1$ to $6$. Amelie and Bob each choose three slips from the hat without replacing any of the slips. Each of them adds up the numbers on his or her slips.

Determine the largest possible difference between Amelie's total and Bob's total. Explain how you found this difference.

cemc-galois-2006-01b.prompt:

List all possible groups of three slips that Amelie can choose so that her total is one more than Bob's total.

cemc-galois-2006-01c.prompt:
A hat contains six slips of paper numbered from $1$ to $6$. Amelie and Bob each choose three slips from the hat without replacing any of the slips. Each of them adds up the numbers on his or her slips.

Explain why it is impossible for Amelie and Bob to have the same total no matter which three slips each chooses.
cemc-galois-2006-01c.answer: Their totals add to $1 + \cdots + 6 = 21$, which is odd, so they can't be equal.

cemc-galois-2006-04a.prompt: When the number $14$ has its digits reversed to form the number $41$, it is increased by $27$. Determine all $2$-digit numbers which are increased by $27$ when their digits are reversed.

cemc-galois-2006-04b.prompt:
Choose any three-digit integer $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$ whose digits are all different. (When an integer is written in terms of its digits as $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$, it means the integer is $100a + 10b + c$.)

Reverse the order of the digits to get a new three-digit integer $\underline{c}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{a}$. Subtract the smaller of these integers from the larger to obtain a three-digit integer $\underline{r}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{t}$, where $r$ is allowed to be $0$. Reverse the order of the digits of this integer to get the integer $\underline{t}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{r}$. Prove that, no matter what three-digit integer $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$ you start with, $\underline{r}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{t} + \underline{t}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{r} = 1089$.
cemc-galois-2006-04b.answer: The difference is $99k$ with $k = |a - c| \in \{1, \dots, 9\}$, whose digits are $k - 1,\ 9,\ 10 - k$; reversing and adding gives $100 \cdot 9 + 10 \cdot 18 + 9 = 1089$.
